name: Felly Club
vision: To establish Felly Club as the premier tech-enabled mentorship ecosystem, empowering individuals to connect with accomplished mentors, gain personalized guidance, and accelerate progress in their chosen fields. By leveraging advanced analytics and fostering trust, the platform delivers meaningful mentor–mentee experiences and builds a scalable community that supports long-term personal and professional growth.
problem: The global mentorship landscape is fragmented and opaque — aspiring individuals across Sport, Entrepreneurship, Business, and Entertainment struggle to identify credible, accessible mentors through standardised discovery mechanisms, while accomplished professionals lack a structured, trustworthy channel to monetize their expertise with transparent pricing, scheduling, and quality assurance.
value_proposition:
Felly Club is the first cross-domain, admin-curated mentorship marketplace spanning Sport, Entrepreneurship, Business, and Entertainment — verticals that established competitors (MentorCruise, GrowthMentor, ADPList) do not serve. Unlike transactional platforms (Clarity.fm, Cameo) or free models with inconsistent quality (ADPList), Felly Club delivers a full session lifecycle — from mentor discovery and domain-verified trust signals through escrow-backed booking, integrated video delivery, post-session ratings, and admin-mediated dispute resolution with session recordings.

For mentees, this means a single platform to find credible, vetted mentors across niche domains with transparent pricing, multi-currency support (INR, USD, CHF, EUR), and structured scheduling — eliminating the fragmentation and opacity that defines the current landscape. For mentors, it provides a trustworthy monetisation channel with flexible pricing, automated payouts, and data-driven performance insights. For the platform, the admin-curated supply model ensures quality over quantity while the commission-based revenue model (10–20%) aligns platform success with mentor and mentee outcomes.

target_users.goal: Discover domain-verified mentors, book one-on-one video sessions, and receive personalized guidance to accelerate personal and professional growth
target_users.frustration: No standardised discovery for domain-specific mentors; opaque pricing and quality indicators; high friction in scheduling, payment, and session delivery
target_users.context: Individuals in India, Switzerland, USA, and Germany seeking mentorship in Sport, Entrepreneurship, Business, or Entertainment via web or mobile

target_users.goal: Monetize expertise through structured one-on-one video mentorship sessions with flexible pricing and availability management
target_users.frustration: No trustworthy platform to offer guidance at scale; lack of structured scheduling, payment collection, and reputation-building tools; no data-driven insights on session performance
target_users.context: Domain-verified professionals onboarded by platform admin, managing availability calendars and accepting session requests across multiple time zones

target_users.goal: Curate a high-quality mentor marketplace by managing onboarding, quality assurance, dispute resolution, financial operations, and platform analytics
target_users.frustration: Manual processes for mentor verification, dispute handling, and payout management; no unified dashboard for platform-wide KPIs and operational oversight
target_users.context: Felly Club operations team using web-based admin portal to manage all platform activities including user lifecycle, sessions, payments, and content

competitors.name: MentorCruise
strengths: Established subscription-based model with 1000+ vetted mentors
Strong in tech, business, and career development verticals
Structured long-term mentorship with ongoing chat and session support
weaknesses: Focused primarily on tech and business — no coverage for Sport or Entertainment
Subscription model limits casual or one-off session seekers

competitors.name: Clarity.fm
strengths: Pay-per-minute model lowers entry barrier for quick consultations
Wide range of business and startup experts
Instant scheduling without complex booking workflows
weaknesses: No domain verification or curated quality assurance framework
Per-minute billing discourages deeper mentorship relationships
No session recording, dispute resolution, or trust mechanisms

competitors.name: GrowthMentor
strengths: Vetted growth and marketing mentors with community-driven quality signals
Active Slack community for peer networking
weaknesses: Narrow focus on growth marketing and product — no Sport or Entertainment
Subscription-only model with no pay-per-session option
Limited to English-speaking markets; no multi-currency support

competitors.name: ADPList
strengths: Free mentorship platform with 20,000+ mentors in design and tech
Low barrier to entry for mentees
weaknesses: Free model creates sustainability concerns and inconsistent mentor commitment
Focused on design and tech — no coverage for Sport, Business, or Entertainment
No payment infrastructure, escrow, or structured revenue model for mentors

competitors.name: Cameo (adjacent)
strengths: Strong brand in celebrity and entertainment interactions
Large roster of public figures across sports and entertainment
weaknesses: Transactional, not mentorship — short video messages, not structured sessions
No scheduling, session management, or ongoing mentor-mentee relationships
No quality assurance, ratings-based matching, or dispute resolution

market_size.tam: ~$1.53B (global mentoring software market, 2025) growing to ~$4.92B by 2035 at 12.4% CAGR
market_size.sam: ~$970M (mentorship marketplace and platform segment, 2026) — platforms enabling 1:1 paid mentorship sessions with booking, payment, and video infrastructure
market_size.som: ~$5–15M achievable within 3 years — targeting curated mentorship in Sport, Entrepreneurship, Business, and Entertainment across India, Switzerland, USA, and Germany
market_size.note: Market sizing derived from Research Nester (2025) and Research & Markets (2026) reports on the global mentoring software market. SAM scoped to marketplace platforms (excluding enterprise mentoring software). SOM estimated based on target geography penetration (4 countries) and niche category focus (4 verticals) with admin-curated supply model constraining initial growth rate.

differentiators: Cross-domain coverage spanning Sport, Entrepreneurship, Business, and Entertainment — most competitors focus narrowly on tech and business verticals
Admin-curated, domain-verified mentor marketplace with verified badges, LinkedIn/portfolio validation, and proof-of-expertise documentation ensuring trust and quality
Full session lifecycle management — from discovery through booking, escrow payment, video session delivery, ratings, and dispute resolution with session recordings
Multi-geography and multi-currency support (INR, USD, CHF, EUR) targeting India, Switzerland, USA, and Germany from MVP launch
risks: Mentor supply constraints — admin-curated onboarding creates a quality-gated supply bottleneck; early marketplace liquidity depends on Felly Club’s ability to attract accomplished professionals in 4 niche verticals
Marketplace cold-start problem — two-sided marketplace requires simultaneous mentor supply and mentee demand; achieving critical mass in each geography and category is the primary growth risk
Competitive pressure from free platforms (ADPList) and established subscription players (MentorCruise, GrowthMentor) who already have network effects and mentor ecosystems
Regulatory complexity — operating across 4 jurisdictions (EU/GDPR, India/TPDP, USA, Switzerland) with multi-currency payments requires significant compliance investment
Fixed-budget delivery risk — €125,000 budget for a full-stack marketplace (web, mobile, admin portal, video, payments, analytics) creates scope-quality tension across 16-week delivery timeline

product_profile.rationale: Primary user (mentee) is a general consumer seeking mentorship with expectations of intuitive, mobile-first UX, onboarding flows, and progressive disclosure. Mentors are professionals but interact through simplified session management. Admin uses a guided web portal.

Platform delivers across three channels — responsive web app (Next.js/Vercel), mobile app (React Native iOS and Android), and admin portal (web). BRD Sprint 1 explicitly includes design system and component library creation. Accessibility at browser and mobile version compatibility level.

Two-sided marketplace with three distinct personas (Mentee, Mentor, Admin) each having different journeys, incentives, dashboards, and feature access. Mentees discover and book; mentors manage availability and receive payouts; admin curates supply and resolves disputes. Maps directly to marketplace pattern (buyer, seller, ops).

Targets 4 countries from MVP launch (India, Switzerland, USA, Germany). Requires multi-currency support (INR, USD, CHF, EUR), GDPR compliance (EU), TPDP compliance (India), and timezone management for cross-border session scheduling.

Consumes and coordinates 7+ external services: Zoom (video), PayU or Stripe (payments), KeyCloak (IAM), Twilio SendGrid (email), FCM (push), Strapi (CMS), Elasticsearch (search). Bidirectional flows for session recording callbacks, payment webhooks, and calendar events.

Full primary flows for all 3 personas, production-grade with error handling, analytics, and compliance. 16-week delivery targeting paying customers across 4 geographies. Not a POC or MVP stub — this is a market-launch product with real payment processing and regulatory compliance.

EdTech and mentorship marketplace in the professional services vertical. Moderate domain rules — session lifecycle management, mentor credentialing, professional standards for expertise verification. Not as heavily regulated as BFSI or healthcare but has PCI DSS (payments) and GDPR/TPDP (data privacy) obligations.

nfr_profile.rationale: Customer-facing marketplace with real financial transactions (escrow, payouts, refunds). Failure impacts user experience, financial operations, and platform trust. PP-3 level 5 (multi-sided platform) means failure affects multiple stakeholder groups simultaneously. Monitoring, alerting, and incident response needed.

BRD specifies KeyCloak for centralised IAM with MFA capability, RBAC, JWT-based API access, AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, and PCI DSS compliance via gateway tokenisation. Matches Business Grade security posture. PP-7 level 3 does not trigger enterprise-grade requirements.

BRD NFR-01 targets under 3 second page load; NFR-02 targets under 500ms API response at 95th percentile. Redis caching for session and search, Elasticsearch for mentor discovery. PP-6 level 3 (Market-Ready) confirms need for performance optimisation for competitive UX.

BRD NFR-05 targets 99.5% uptime (excluding scheduled maintenance). Horizontal scaling on Vercel and cloud infrastructure. Blue-green deployments via GitHub Actions CI/CD. PP-4 level 3 (multi-country) confirms need for standard availability across timezones.

BRD explicitly requires GDPR (EU — Switzerland, Germany), TPDP (India), PCI DSS (payments), cookie consent, privacy policy, data export, and right-to-deletion. PP-4 level 3 (multi-country) triggers NFR-5 at least 2; actual BRD requirements push to level 3.

BRD NFR-04 requires horizontal scaling. PP-3 level 5 (multi-sided platform) triggers NFR-6 at least 3. Initial target is thousands of users across 4 countries with 4 expertise categories. Designed for 10x growth with load balancing and read replicas.

Platform handles financial data (payment transactions, escrow balances, payout amounts), PII (names, emails, professional credentials), and session recordings (video content with admin-only access). PCI DSS tokenisation required. Field-level access control for recordings (admin-only). Encryption at rest mandatory per BRD NFR-07.

quality_profile.rationale: PP-6 level 3 (Market-Ready) triggers QP-1 at least 3. PP-3 level 5 (multi-sided platform with complex permissions) reinforces need for thorough testing. Multi-currency payments, session lifecycle, and dispute workflows require unit plus integration plus e2e for critical paths. CI runs tests on every PR.

PP-6 level 3 (Market-Ready) with a 16-week delivery by an external team (Nagarro) necessitates enforced standards — linter, formatter, pre-commit hooks, static analysis, PR review with checklist, documented coding conventions. Technical debt management critical given fixed-price engagement.

NFR-5 level 3 (Standard Compliance) triggers QP-3 at least 3. Multi-service architecture (7+ integrations) requires OpenAPI specs, architecture overview, ADRs, and runbooks. External delivery team handover requires comprehensive onboarding documentation.

PP-6 level 3 (Market-Ready) and NFR-4 level 3 (Standard Availability) both trigger QP-4 at least 3. BRD explicitly specifies GitHub Actions CI/CD, Docker containerisation, and managed hosting on Vercel. Multiple environments (dev, staging, prod) with automated database migrations.

NFR-4 level 3 (Standard Availability) triggers QP-5 at least 3. BRD NFR-16 specifies centralised logging, monitoring, tracing, and alerting via cloud-native tooling. Payment processing, session lifecycle, and cross-timezone scheduling require operational visibility dashboards.

BRD specifies browser compatibility (last 2 versions of Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge) and mobile compatibility (last 2 major iOS and Android versions) but does not mention WCAG compliance or formal accessibility standards. PP-1 level 4 (General Consumer) benefits from good accessibility but no regulatory mandate exists in the BRD.

NFR-2 level 3 (Business Grade) triggers QP-7 at least 3. NFR-5 level 3 (Standard Compliance) reinforces need for security scanning. PCI DSS compliance requires dependency auditing and secure coding practices. SAST in CI with secret scanning for API keys (Zoom, payment provider, SendGrid, Firebase).
